risks.title: NAT throughput NFR of 10-15 Mbps is not achievable alongside the other workloads
risks.description: PRD NFR 7.1 demands 10-15 Mbps NAT throughput under good LTE signal. The A7670E is a Cat-1 bis LTE-FDD modem; its practical theoretical ceiling is roughly 10 Mbps down and it is rarely sustained in real networks. Adding SoftAP forwarding, MJPEG video encoding, MQTT, and ESP-SR DSP on the same ESP32-S3 competes directly for the same CPU and memory. The NFR was written without reference to the modem's real ceiling.
risks.mitigation: Measure early with a dedicated throughput harness before committing to the figure. Set a realistic target and renegotiate the NFR with the stakeholder. Do not build the whole product against an unvalidated number.
risks.contingency: Reduce the target to a measured figure and document the gap. Consider deferring MJPEG or ESP-SR to free CPU if the two conflict.

risks.title: PPP data path over UART was unproven on this board
risks.description: PPP had never produced an IP on this device. The earlier attempt failed on a Jio SIM with +CGREG: 0,3, which is a registration symptom rather than a PPP one. TASK-020 retested on the Airtel SIM and has now closed the gap: the data bearer works, the module accepts a PPP dial over UART, and lwIP negotiates LCP/IPCP to phase RUNNING with local=100.76.140.112 and gateway=10.64.64.64, held stable and reproduced on a cold boot.
risks.impact: If LCP/IPCP fails, REQ-004 NAT routing is not achievable and the product descopes or changes modem. Until it is demonstrated, treat NAT routing as unproven rather than assumed.
risks.mitigation: All three questions are now answered and the risk is closed as verified. RETIRED: 'PPP is unreachable because esp_modem's A7670 PPP path is USB-only' - the module accepts a PPP dial over UART and completes the handshake. RETIRED: 'the SIM/network blocks data' - Airtel assigns a real CGNAT address. RESOLVED: LCP/IPCP completes and the ESP32 receives an IP. This required three fixes recorded in BUG-006 (a post-CONNECT settle delay, tcpip_init() for the receive path, and the mandatory core lock). What remains downstream is REQ-004: NAT routing over the PPP interface, which this test does not prove.
risks.contingency: No longer applicable to PPP reachability. RET-002 is closed by TEST-020. The remaining REQ-004 exposure is scope and throughput, not feasibility: the CGNAT address 100.x.x.x is not reachable inbound, and the PRD's 10-15 Mbps target is unmeasured on LTE.

risks.title: Audio hardware presence and wiring are unconfirmed, blocking telephony and voice
risks.description: The PRD requires I2S MEMS microphone (INMP441), I2S DAC (MAX98357A) and full-duplex audio through the A7670E PCM channel. The Waveshare ESP32-S3-A7670E-4G board we actually have has not been shown to have these parts fitted or correctly wired. nomad-sentinel TASKS.md 1.11 records the audio path as UNSUPPORTED. Outgoing calls work for control signalling but full duplex audio was never proven; the earlier 'user heard audio' result needs re-examination because it may have been ringback rather than the far end.
risks.mitigation: Physically inspect the board and confirm whether an I2S mic and amp are populated. Run a loopback test (record from mic, play to DAC) before committing any voice tasks. Update the PRD's hardware table to match the real BOM.
risks.contingency: Descope FR-7 entirely (ESP-SR voice dialling) and REQ-017's full-duplex requirement. Control-signalling-only telephony remains viable via ATD/ATA/ATH.

risks.title: ESP-SR sub-800ms latency target is unvalidated and may be unreachable
risks.description: PRD NFR 7.2 requires wake-word and command recognition under 800 ms using ESP-SR WakeNet + MultiNet. This has never been measured on this board. ESP-SR on ESP32-S3 is plausible but the figure was asserted without a benchmark.
risks.mitigation: Benchmark ESP-SR latency as an isolated spike before building the contacts UI. Measure wake-word detection latency separately from command classification latency.
risks.contingency: Relax the NFR to the measured value, or scope voice recognition down to fixed-phrase dialing only.

risks.title: TLS on the cellular path is unverified, blocking the security NFR
risks.description: PRD NFR 4.4 mandates TLS 1.2/1.3 for all cloud connectivity. The working socket path today is plaintext AT+CIPOPEN to port 1883. AT+CSSLCFG, SNI and certificate installation have not been tested on firmware A011B04A7670M7_F. Plaintext MQTT carrying credentials and telemetry is a Rule 27 problem and cannot ship.
risks.mitigation: Test AT+CSSLCFG with SNI against port 8883 as an early isolated experiment. A full MQTT-over-TLS handshake over a CIPSEND socket is more complex than the plaintext path and may justify using the TinyGSM A7672x client library instead of hand-rolled AT.
risks.contingency: Publish plaintext only in a lab build behind an explicit INSECURE_TRANSPORT flag, and document it as non-shippable.

risks.title: SD card works under Arduino but is blocked under ESP-IDF
risks.description: The Arduino path writes, reads and deletes on a 3.98 GB FAT32 card with SD_MMC.setPins(5,4,6). nomad-sentinel/TASKS.md 1.7 records every card command failing with err=0x107 under ESP-IDF. GPIO46 is documented as not a usable card-detect line. This is a genuine framework discrepancy that must be resolved before SD features are scheduled, and it interacts with RISK-007.
risks.mitigation: Diagnose the 0x107 difference. It may be a clock or pin-drive configuration issue, or the Arduino core may be masking a marginal socket. Logged as BUG-001.
risks.contingency: If SD is unreliable, use LittleFS on flash and descope snapshot storage.

risks.title: Device runs seven FreeRTOS tasks plus NAT, video and DSP on two cores
risks.description: The PRD allocates 7 tasks across 2 cores with NAT forwarding, MJPEG encoding and speech DSP. Free heap on this class of device is 2.46 MB internal plus PSRAM, and NAT tables plus frame buffers plus ESP-SR models are all competing. nomad-sentinel 1.3 measured only 2.46 MB free heap internally.
risks.mitigation: Enforce task stack sizing discipline, place NAT and modem on core 0, keep video and audio on core 1, and monitor free heap and minimum-ever-free-heap in the dashboard. Define a memory budget per subsystem before implementation.
risks.contingency: Reduce concurrent feature load: NAT and video cannot both run at full rate; make the dashboard report the conflict.

risks.title: GitHub personal access token was shared in plaintext and remains valid
risks.description: A live ghp_ token with repo scope was pasted in plaintext in the session. The user elected to keep it valid. It has repo scope over the whole account, so a leak allows full repository write and read. It is not written to any file in this repository and keyring auth is used instead.
risks.mitigation: Revoke and regenerate the token at https://github.com/settings/tokens. Prefer gh auth keyring or a fine-grained token scoped to this repository only. Never place it in .env committed to the repo. 2026-09-29 update: the token was never written to any file in this repository, confirmed by a full scan of all 61 blobs in the published repo. The repository is now PUBLIC, so the token must not be granted any scope that the world can use. Recommended: revoke and reissue with least privilege. Owner declined to rotate at time of writing; this risk is accepted and remains open.
risks.contingency: If the token is found abused, revoke immediately and audit repository access logs.

risks.title: Cellular LBS accuracy is coarse and operator-dependent
risks.description: LBS returned 18.481703, 73.897415 with a 550 m accuracy radius. This is a fallback, not a tracking solution. It also depends on the carrier providing the location service and on the 4G patch antenna being physically attached, which is easy to forget and silently degrades to +CLBS: 9.
risks.mitigation: Always report accuracy and source. Warn in the dashboard when CSQ is low. Make antenna state an explicit documented precondition.
risks.contingency: Degrade to GNSS-only and mark position as unavailable rather than reporting a stale or misleading fix.

risks.title: Public repository exposes hardware design and product roadmap
risks.description: The repository was made public on 2026-09-29 to enable GitHub Pages on the free plan. It now publishes the board pinout, the modem AT command bring-up notes, and the unbuilt product roadmap.
risks.impact: A third party could learn the hardware design, the SIM/operator details and the feature plan before launch.
risks.mitigation: Real IMEI, phone numbers and broker credentials are redacted and enforced by secrets_scan.py. Board pinouts are public on the vendor's own documentation anyway. If the roadmap must stay confidential before launch, move docs/product and LESSONS_LEARNED.md to a private repo and keep only the dashboards public.
